goal: Say what is where, and ask and give simple directions around a house or town.

vocab.meaning: to be, to exist (things, plants); to have

grammar.title: あります / います — "there is"
grammar.pattern: N が あります (things) / N が います (people, animals)
grammar.explanation: Japanese has two verbs for "there is". Use あります for things that don't move by themselves — books, buildings, and also plants and trees. Use います for people and animals. The particle が marks the thing that exists. They change like any ます verb: ありません / ありました, いません / いました.
notes: Trees and flowers use あります, even though they are alive.
あります can also mean "have": 時間がありません = I don't have time.

grammar.title: Place に N が あります — "In the room there is a TV"
grammar.pattern: Place に N が あります / います
grammar.explanation: To say what is in a place, start with the place and に, then the thing and が, then あります or います: 部屋にテレビがあります (There is a TV in the room). に here means "in / at" for where something exists. This pattern introduces something new — the listener didn't know about the TV before. To ask, use 何 or だれ with が: 部屋に何がありますか.
notes: Use に, not で, for where something exists: 部屋でテレビがあります is wrong.
何[なに]がありますか asks about things; だれがいますか asks about people.

grammar.title: N は Place に あります — "The TV is in the room"
grammar.pattern: N は Place に あります / います
grammar.explanation: When you already know which thing you mean and want to say where it is, make the thing the topic with は and put the place after it: テレビは部屋にあります (The TV is in the room). This is how you answer "Where is …?": トイレはどこにありますか. Compare: 部屋にテレビがあります tells you what is in the room; テレビは部屋にあります tells you where the TV is.
notes: In conversation you can shorten it with です: トイレはあそこです.
Use います for people and animals here too: 田中さんは二階にいます.

grammar.title: Position words — on, under, in front of…
grammar.pattern: N の 上 / 下 / 中 / 外 / 前 / 後ろ / 横 / 隣 / 近く に
grammar.meaning: on / under / in / outside / in front of / behind / beside / next to / near N
grammar.explanation: In Japanese, position words are nouns, so they come after the thing they relate to, joined with の: 机の上 is literally "the desk's top" — on the desk. Then add に to say something is there: 机の上に本があります. Think of it as reading backwards: 駅の前 = "station's front" = in front of the station. Useful words: 上 (on), 下 (under), 中 (in), 外 (outside), 前 (in front), 後ろ (behind), 横 (beside), 隣 (next to), 近く (near).
notes: 隣 is for two similar things side by side (house next to house, person next to person); 横 is simply "at the side".
Between A and B: A と B の間 (あいだ).
近く is a noun ("nearby"); 近い is an adjective ("is near").

grammar.title: や〜など — "A, B and so on"
grammar.explanation: や joins nouns like と, but with a difference. と lists everything: 本とペン means "a book and a pen" — that's all. や gives just a few examples: 本やペン means "books, pens and things like that". You can add など ("and so on") after the last item to make that even clearer: 本やペンなどがあります.
notes: と = the complete list; や = some examples from a longer list.
Particles like が and を come after など: ペンなどがあります.

grammar.title: 何か / だれか / 何も — "something", "someone", "nothing"
grammar.pattern: 何か / だれか + question ・ 何も / だれも + negative
grammar.explanation: Add か to a question word and it becomes "some-": 何か (something), だれか (someone). Add も instead and use a negative verb, and it becomes "no-": 何もありません (there's nothing), だれもいません (there's nobody). The particles が and を are usually dropped after 何か / だれか (何かありますか is more natural than 何かがありますか), and they are never used with 何も / だれも: say 何もありません, not 何もがありません. Note the reading: 何か is なにか and 何も is なにも.
notes: 何も and だれも always need a negative: 何も食べませんでした = I didn't eat anything.
何か飲みませんか = Would you like something to drink?
何 is read なに here, not なん.

reading.title: 私[わたし]の部屋[へや] — My room
reading.text: 私[わたし]の部屋[へや]は二階[にかい]にあります。あまり広[ひろ]くないですが、明[あか]るい部屋[へや]です。窓[まど]の前[まえ]に机[つくえ]があります。机[つくえ]の上[うえ]にパソコンや本[ほん]などがあります。ベッドは机[つくえ]の右[みぎ]にあります。ベッドの上[うえ]に猫[ねこ]がいます。名前[なまえ]はミケです。テレビは一階[いっかい]にあります。家[いえ]の近[ちか]くに公園[こうえん]があります。公園[こうえん]にきれいな池[いけ]があります。
reading.en: My room is on the second floor. It isn't very big, but it's a bright room. There is a desk in front of the window. On the desk there are a computer, books and so on. The bed is to the right of the desk. There is a cat on the bed. Its name is Mike. The TV is on the first floor. There is a park near my house. There is a pretty pond in the park.
